claim_wording: INE's IMC 2024 report records a national unemployment rate of 8.0% for 2024, down from 10.3% in 2023.
claim_type: documented fact from official statistical report
status: supported within stated source and definition
what_evidence_supports: INE report and government labour summary report the 8.0% rate and 10.3% in 2023
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish job security, wages, underemployment, informality, job matching, or equal outcomes across islands and groups
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: 2025 estimates from other sources use a different reference year and may use different methods
next_verification_step: Extract definitions and municipality/age/sex tables from the full INE report; compare like-for-like series

claim_wording: INE's IMC 2024 reporting gives a labour-underutilisation rate of 28.4% and youth unemployment (ages 15–24) of 20.1% for 2024.
claim_type: documented fact from official statistical summary
status: supported within stated source and definition
confidence: high for reported figures; interpretation needs care
what_evidence_supports: Official labour-market summary reports both figures
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not mean 28.4% are unemployed; labour underutilisation is a broader measure with its own definition; does not identify each person's barriers
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Need inspect INE definitions, disaggregation and confidence/precision notes
next_verification_step: Extract exact definitions and subgroup tables from INE IMC 2024

claim_wording: ADECO's March 2026 Essential Consumption Index estimated a monthly basket of about CVE 33,156 in Praia, CVE 34,909 on Sal, and CVE 24,856 on São Vicente for one healthy individual.
claim_type: reported claim by named consumer association, relayed by local press
confidence: medium-high that these are the published estimates; limited as a universal affordability measure
what_evidence_supports: ADECO's published update and Expresso das Ilhas report the island-specific figures
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish a universal cost of living, a family budget, actual spending for all households, or wage adequacy for all household types; basket and rent assumptions vary by place
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Underlying calculations, basket quantities, rent assumptions, sampling/price collection and wage definitions need checking; coverage is limited to three locations
next_verification_step: Read the original ADECO calculation reports and document basket assumptions before using the figures comparatively

claim_wording: Inforpress reported from IMC 2024 results that 43.9% of Cabo Verdean households did not have enough water to meet their needs in 2024.
claim_type: reported claim attributed to official survey, via news agency
status: secondary report; primary table verification pending
what_evidence_supports: Inforpress explicitly attributes the figure to INE IMC 2024; it reports higher incidence in rural areas
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish water quality, continuity, affordability, duration of interruptions, or the exact cause; not every island or household necessarily has the same experience
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Need the exact survey question, definition, disaggregation, sampling precision, and primary table
next_verification_step: Find and inspect the matching IMC 2024 water-access table and compare with utility/service data

claim_wording: Inforpress's retrospective reported that irregular maritime links affected Brava's supply of essential goods during 2025, including food and other necessities.
geographic_scope: Brava; 2025, with links to Fogo and Santiago
confidence: medium as evidence of reported incidents, low for prevalence or causation
what_evidence_supports: Local reporting describes supply disruptions and reports from merchants and local context
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish a national pattern, the frequency/length of every interruption, the size of price effects, or that transport alone caused every shortage
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Need port/operator schedules, freight volumes, price series, merchant records and independent local accounts
next_verification_step: Triangulate with transport operators, port data, local authorities and additional reporting from Brava

claim_wording: The World Bank's July 2026 economic update reports 6.3% real GDP growth in 2025 and identifies weak, costly inter-island transport as a constraint on broader economic integration.
confidence: medium-high for what the World Bank reports; causal interpretation needs full report
what_evidence_supports: World Bank summary gives growth figure and describes connectivity constraints on markets, costs and diversification
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not show that all households benefited equally from growth, or quantify the causal effect of each transport bottleneck
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Need full report, transport service/reliability/cost series, and distributional data by island, sector, gender and age
next_verification_step: Review full economic update and gather island-specific service and price evidence

claim_wording: The World Bank's 2025 climate-report summary states that imports account for 80% of domestic food consumption in Cabo Verde.
status: reported; definition and year need confirmation
what_evidence_supports: World Bank summary explicitly gives the 80% figure and links import dependence with climate and supply-chain vulnerability
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish the share for every food category or year, or directly measure household food insecurity
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Need full report definition, reference year, commodity coverage and corroborating trade/agriculture data
next_verification_step: Inspect full Country Climate and Development Report and compare with customs, agriculture and food-balance data

claim_wording: INE's July 2026 CPI release reports national inflation measures, but those national measures alone cannot establish affordability for each island or income group.
status: supported as a scope limitation; detailed data extraction pending
what_evidence_supports: INE publishes national CPI measures and time comparisons
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not directly measure household purchasing power, rent burden, regional basket differences or the adequacy of minimum wages
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Need CPI components, island-level price data and household income/expenditure data for distributional analysis
next_verification_step: Extract CPI values and component contributions; compare with ADECO's locally constructed basket while keeping methods distinct

claim_wording: Cabo Verde's water, food, energy and climate risks are interlinked in the World Bank and IMF climate diagnostics.
geographic_scope: National; climate, energy, water and food systems
status: supported as a documented institutional analysis; detailed claim review pending
what_evidence_supports: World Bank and IMF diagnostics describe drought/water scarcity, energy-intensive desalination, imported fuel/food exposure and agricultural constraints
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish the impact on each household, the current severity in every island, or that any one intervention is effective
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Need technical report details, updated island-level water/energy data, and local lived-experience evidence
next_verification_step: Extract specific technical claims and match them to current public data and locally reported experience

claim_wording: Current evidence gathered in this first pass is insufficient to rank housing, healthcare staffing, education-to-work, unpaid care, waste, media influence, or religious-organisational harm across Cabo Verde.
confidence: high for this repository's present coverage, not a claim that data do not exist
what_evidence_supports: The first-pass source set contains only partial or indirect coverage of these topics
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish that the problems are absent, present at a particular scale, or ranked below other challenges
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Targeted primary statistics, relevant local reporting and ethical local consultation have not yet been systematically gathered for each topic
next_verification_step: Build separate source searches and claim sets for each topic; for influence-related concerns assess observable practices and effects rather than identity or belief

claim_wording: INE's 2024 household living-conditions report includes data on water sufficiency and drinking-water practices, including a reported 46.5% of households drinking untreated water.
claim_type: documented fact from official statistical report
status: primary source identified; exact table and question wording should be checked before final publication
what_evidence_supports: INE's official IMC 2024 living-conditions report contains the relevant drinking-water table and urban/rural breakdown
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish that all untreated water was contaminated, that all households experienced unsafe water, or that water quality was laboratory-tested in this statistic
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Confirm table denominator, question wording, whether categories overlap, and sampling notes; distinguish reported household practice from measured quality
next_verification_step: Inspect full report pages/tables and record exact question and category definitions

claim_wording: WHO's Cabo Verde Country Cooperation Strategy 2024–2028 identifies equitable distribution of qualified health workers across the inhabited islands as a challenge and reports historical staffing data.
geographic_scope: Cabo Verde; strategy published 2024, figures include earlier years
status: supported as a statement of WHO's strategy; current status requires newer data
confidence: high for what the strategy states; low for current staffing conditions
what_evidence_supports: WHO strategy describes health workforce and quality of care as priorities and notes distribution challenges
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish present-day staffing levels, waiting times, service quality, patient outcomes, or shortages in every island/facility
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Extract historical reference year and definitions; compare with current Ministry of Health workforce, facility, waiting-time and referral data
next_verification_step: Review strategy tables and seek current administrative statistics and island-specific reporting

claim_wording: In October 2025, Inforpress reported that the National Association of Cape Verdean Municipalities described a significant housing deficit in quantity and quality.
confidence: medium as evidence that the association made the statement; low for the size of the deficit
what_evidence_supports: Inforpress attributes the assessment to the association's president and reports municipal funding constraints
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not quantify the number of homes needed, identify affected groups or municipalities, or establish the current deficit independently
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Need census housing-stock data, household formation, rent/price data, overcrowding, informal housing and programme completion outcomes
next_verification_step: Compare the statement with INE census/housing data and current municipal/national programme results

claim_type: documented fact about an official announcement
geographic_scope: Praia, São Vicente and Sal; snapshot as reported 2025-04-09
confidence: high for what the announcement stated; low for present status or impact
what_evidence_supports: Government announcement describes a proposed rent-to-own model and construction counts at that time
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not establish legal finalisation, completion, eligibility, allocation, affordability, or a reduction in housing need
contrary_evidence_or_gaps: Find programme legislation, procurement/construction updates, completion and allocation counts, affordability rules and beneficiary outcomes
next_verification_step: Verify implementation and completed/occupied units through subsequent official records and independent reporting
